title: Dream star Angel Reese vows 'we'll be back' after Game 7 loss vs. Valkyries in WNBA Finals - CBS Sports
description: Reese was limited to eight points on Saturday night as Atlanta fell short of a title against Golden State
body:
Reese was limited to eight points on Saturday night as Atlanta fell short of a title against Golden State
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Angel Reese was, understandably, devastated as her third WNBA season came to a close on Saturday night in a Game 7 loss in the WNBA Finals to the Golden State Valkyries, 68-63. But even with the heartache, the Dream forward -- who was traded from the Chicago Sky to Atlanta in April -- expressed appreciation for the Dream organization and her teammates for the best season of her young WNBA career."They changed my life, and I'm just so grateful for them, and I'm so thankful for them," she said. "And it is tough in the moment, but we'll be back. And I always say delayed, not denied, and this is only Year 3."Reese was named Defensive Player of the Year this season, made her third All-Star team and was named to the All-WNBA second team as well, which makes her eligible for the EPIC extension. She set the single-season rebounding record, single-season double-double record and single-game rebounding record. Her offensive game improved drastically under the guidance of Dream coach Karl Smesko, who worked directly with Reese to re-make her shot.But she struggled in Game 7, with just eight points. She shot 3 of 7 from the field (42.9%), 1 of 3 from outside (33.3%) and 1 of 3 from the line (33.3%). Reese had 12 rebounds -- nine offensive, three defensive -- as well as one assist, one steal and two blocks, but her four turnovers were very costly. She had zero shot attempts in the fourth quarter and only got to the line once in the final frame. It was a performance that will likely haunt her in the offseason, but she kept things in perspective after the game.
"I'm really proud of the year that I had. I mean, I've done a lot of great things this year, but I wouldn't be able to do it without this group," Reese said. "We've won a lot of great games, and to come all the way to the Finals with this group, I mean, it says a lot. Not a lot of people have this opportunity to do it. And, like I said, I'd do it all over again with this same group, just battling with them every single day, I love these girls. I love the coaches. I think it also sucks because our fan base back home poured into us so much this year, and we really wanted to do it for them. But we're forever grateful, and like I said, we'll be back."
        
            
                'I stayed patient': How Finals MVP Gabby Williams made history in Game 7 to fuel Valkyries to WNBA title
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
In the series, Reese averaged 14.7 points and 12.6 rebounds per game. In Game 2, she had a record-setting 30-point, 16-rebound showing, and followed that up with 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 4. She had four double-doubles in the series. However, she was held to eight or fewer points in three of the Dream's four losses.She is looking forward to a full offseason working with Smesko and better learning the Dream's system, and knows that her first playoff run will help her grow in the long run. After a couple of years in Chicago that were filled with off-court change and roster turnover, she has finally found stability and success in Atlanta.
"Honestly, I really enjoy just being around a group of girls that just come to work every day and want to work and want to get better, and they push me to be better," she said. "I'm a young player and I'm very vocal, but I think they really help me mature in different ways that I haven't really been challenged."

title: Mets legend Jerry Koosman dies at 83: Pitcher helped New York win 1969 World Series - CBS Sports
description: The Mets inducted Koosman into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his No. 36 in 2021
body:
The Mets inducted Koosman into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his No. 36 in 2021
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
New York Mets team Hall of Famer and two-time All-Star Jerry Koosman died Sunday morning in Osceola, Wisconsin, the team announced. He was 83. The Mets say Koosman battled multiple illnesses before his death."Kooz was one of the greatest pitchers in team history and a beloved member of the Mets family," Mets owners Alex and Steve Cohen said in a statement. "The 1969 Miracle Mets were filled with heroes, and the special southpaw from Appleton, Minnesota, was central to their success. He was a fierce competitor on the field, and respected teammate in the clubhouse. His legendary performance in the World Series helped the Mets secure their first Championship in team history. On behalf of the entire Mets organization, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Jerry's family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him."The Mets discovered Koosman while he was pitching for the United States Army and signed him to a contract in August 1964. He made his MLB debut in April 1967 and moved into the rotation full-time the next season. Koosman threw 263 ⅔ innings with a 2.08 ERA as a rookie in 1968, which earned him an All-Star Game selection and MVP votes, and a second-place finish in the Rookie of the Year voting behind Hall of Famer Johnny Bench.In 1969, Koosman was again an All-Star, throwing 241 innings with a 2.28 ERA. He was New York's No. 2 starter in the postseason between Hall of Famers Tom Seaver and Nolan Ryan. Koosman made two starts for the Miracle Mets in the World Series, including the Game 5 clincher against the Baltimore Orioles. He allowed three runs in the complete game win and recorded all but one possible out in his two World Series starts.From 1968-76, Koosman was simply one of the best pitchers in the game, pitching to a 2.94 ERA and averaging 223 innings per season. The Mets traded him to the Minnesota Twins for Jesse Orosco in December 1978 and Koosman finished his career with stints for the Twins (1979-81), Chicago White Sox (1981-83), and Philadelphia Phillies (1984-85).Koosman retired following the 1985 season with a 222-209 record and a 3.36 ERA that is 39th among AL/NL pitchers with at least 3,500 career innings. He ranks 35th all-time in strikeouts (2,556), 40th all-time in starts (527), 48th all-time in innings (3,839 ⅓), and 77th all-time in pitching WAR (57.0). Koosman went to two All-Star Games and finished second to Randy Jones in the 1976 Cy Young voting.The Mets inducted Koosman into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his No. 36 in 2021. His 140 wins are the most in franchise history among left-handers and third in team history overall, behind Seaver (198) and Dwight Gooden (157). Koosman is second in Mets history in innings (behind Seaver) and third in strikeouts (behind Seaver and Gooden).Koosman fell off the Baseball Writers Association of America's Hall of Fame ballot in 1991, his first year of eligibility.

title: NFL Thanksgiving schedule: Lions announce halftime show performer for game vs. Bears - CBS Sports
description: Wu-Tang Clan will perform at halftime for a huge holiday game
body:
Wu-Tang Clan will perform at halftime for a huge holiday game
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This season, the Detroit Lions Thanksgiving Day game will feature Wu-Tang Clan as the halftime show performer. The 87th annual Thanksgiving Day Classic will take place on Thursday, Nov. 26 at Ford Field, when the Lions host the Chicago Bears.Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET, and the game, as well as the halftime show, will be broadcast on CBS and streamed on Paramount+."Our Thanksgiving Day Classic is one of the greatest traditions in sports, and Wu-Tang Clan is one of the greatest performers in music," Rich Haddad, Lions President and CEO said. "We are thrilled to have Wu-Tang headlining our Thanksgiving halftime show and grateful to Marshall and Paul for their partnership."Wu-Tang Clan's influence goes far beyond music and into fashion, film and television. The group is part of the 2026 class of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and they are currently on a farewell tour, Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber.
The group consists of RZA, GZA, Method Man, Raekwon, Ghostface Killah, U-God, Masta Killa, Inspectah Deck, Cappadonna and the late Ol' Dirty Bastard (ODB). They were founded in Staten Island, New York and have released eight albums as a group.This is the second year rapper Eminem and his long-time manager and president of Shady Records Paul Rosenberg have selected the performer and will executive produce the show."We often like to do things that are both exciting and unexpected. A Wu-Tang Clan Thanksgiving performance in Detroit certainly fits that description!" Rosenberg said. "Both Eminem and myself have been Wu fans since the early 90's along with a whole generation of Detroit football fans, and we are honored to bring them to this year's stage."
The Lions have become a Thanksgiving staple, with a long tradition of hosting a game on the holiday dating back to 1934, except for the 1939 to 1944 seasons.

title: Ranking the 10 best women's college basketball players for 2026-27: Can anyone catch Sarah Strong? - CBS Sports
description: With JuJu Watkins back and Hannah Hidalgo off to a strong start, the POTY race is already a thriller
body:
With JuJu Watkins back and Hannah Hidalgo off to a strong start, the POTY race is already a thriller
        
        
                                                                                                            
                                                    By
                                                
                                                            CBS Sports Staff
                                                    
                    
                                    
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    
            
    
        There was a full 14 hours between the end of the WNBA season in Game 7 on Saturday, Oct. 31, in San Francisco and the tip-off of the women's college basketball season in Rome, Italy, on Nov. 1. Hope you enjoyed your offseason, women's hoops fans. The 2026-27 college season got off to a high-scoring start, with Notre Dame beating Villanova 99-75 at the Eternal City Tip-Off behind Hannah Hidalgo's 32 points, seven rebounds, eight assists and three assists. Most other top players will start their seasons on Monday, including JuJu Watkins, who returns to the USC lineup after missing all of last season recovering from an ACL tear. Watkins will make her debut against UNLV at 4 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network and streaming on Paramount+.
        
            
                Women's college basketball rankings: JuJu Watkins has USC at No. 3 in AP Top 25, South Carolina begins on top
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
There are many talented players in Division I, but we compiled a list of the top players to keep an eye on. Without giving away spoilers, here are CBS Sports' top 10 women's college basketball players ahead of the 2026-27 season.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    10. Toby FournierDespite a shaky start last season while facing some tough opponents, Duke turned things around and won both the ACC regular season and conference tournament titles before making it to the Elite Eight. Fournier was the key component to this success as the team's leader in scoring, rebounding and blocks. After not starting any games as a freshman and still winning ACC rookie of the year, the 6-foot-2 forward thrived as a starter last season with 17.3 points on 52.5% shooting from the field, 7.9 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game. 
Fournier demonstrates her power and athleticism with her ability to finish at the rim. In fact, her two-handed dunk has become a signature move for her during pre-game warmups. However, she also has great footwork and her high motor makes her dangerous in transition. Her 6-foot-5 wingspan and basketball IQ also make her a threat on defense.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    9. Olivia OlsonThe Wolverines are fresh off a historic 28–7 overall season and a trip to the Elite Eight with Olson as their leading scorer and rebounder. The 6-foot-1 guard averaged 18.9 points per game as a sophomore while shooting 46.8% as a crafty and versatile scorer. Her body control, even mid-air, allows her to finish even if she gets bumped by a defender. She is also not afraid to crash the boards, which is clear from her 6.1 boards per contest.One of her most memorable games last season was her career-high 31 points in an 88-86 overtime win against Ohio State on Feb. 25. That performance also included nine rebounds, four assists and, most notably, the game-winner with 3.2 remaining in the extra period.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    8. Audi CrooksCrooks was the top player in the transfer portal this offseason and, now she will be playing her senior year at Oklahoma State. The 6-foot-3 center was averaging more than one point per minute in the first part of last season and she currently holds the longest active Division I women's college basketball streak for consecutive games scoring in double figures. Crooks' only college boxscore with fewer than 10 points was during her very first game as a freshman in 2023. Her size and physical strength, combined with elite footwork, make her a force to be reckoned with in the paint. She wrapped up the 2025-26 campaign as the nation's second leading scorer with 25.8 points per contest while shooting 64.9% from the field. This includes her career-high 47 points while shooting 19 of 25 from the field in a 106-95 win over Indiana on Nov. 30.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    7. Jaloni CambridgeCambridge's sophomore season ended in a loss to Notre Dame in the second round of the NCAA Tournament, but she put on an admirable fight in the defeat with 41 points on 52% shooting from the field while going 5 of 8 from beyond the arc. She is coming off a breakout season and it will be fun to see if she can bring that momentum into her junior year. 
Cambridge scored in double figures in every single game last season, including 21 outings with 20+ points. She averaged 23.2 points per game on 49.4% shooting, which made her the Big Ten's leading scorer and No. 6 in the nation. The 5-foot-7 point guard is quick, efficient and shows up to the court every day with a "whatever it takes" attitude instilled by her dad. Besides her scoring, she also contributed 5.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.9 steals per game.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    6. Joyce EdwardsEdwards is a versatile weapon for South Carolina who impacts the game on both sides of the court. Her speed and high basketball IQ help her turn defense into offense with a strong transition game. She confidently attacks the rim and is able to finish through contact.The 6-foot-3 forward finished her sophomore year averaging a team-high 19.2 points per game while shooting 57.1% from the field. In the process, she set a new South Carolina single-season scoring record with a total of 768 points. Edwards also led the Gamecocks with 1.8 steals per game, along with 1.1 blocks per contest. Coach Dawn Staley has praised her ball-handling skills and even compared her to former Gamecock and current WNBA superstar A'ja Wilson.
"I think Joyce probably can handle the ball a little bit better than A'ja when A'ja was her age," Staley said. "Joyce probably gets a lot of harder scores than A'ja just by mere height. A'ja's got a little bit more height on her."

                            
    
                                                
                    
    5. Madison BookerLet's get this out of the way: Booker had the worst game of her career during the Final Four matchup against UCLA, but that performance by no means defines her as a player. Booker averaged 18.9 points per game while shooting 50.8% from the floor last season. She set a new career high of 40 points while shooting 66.7% in a 100-58 win over Oregon in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. Booker models her game after NBA star Kevin Durant, which clearly reflects through her elite mid-range skills and footwork. She is an athletic forward with a high basketball IQ and the ability to step in as point guard -- which we saw during her freshman year when Rori Harmon was injured. On the other side of the court, Booker uses her physical advantage and quick hands to be disruptive on defense, which is a non-negotiable for anyone who plays for Vic Schaefer. With Harmon now in the WNBA, this will be an exciting year for Booker as she steps into a veteran leadership role.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    4. Mikayla BlakesBlakes is one of the most exciting high-volume scorers in college basketball and has been in the spotlight since her freshman season, which featured two 50+ point games. Her 55 points against Auburn in February 2025 broke Elena Delle Donne's Division I freshman single-game scoring record. As a sophomore last season, Blakes led the nation in scoring with 27.1 points per game, including 12 games in which she scored 30+ points. Her 918 total points set a new NCAA Division I sophomore single-season scoring record. What makes this even more impressive is that Blakes doesn't have to rely on 3-point shooting. She shoots 45.6% from the field but just 35.9% from beyond the arc -- although she is dangerous from anywhere when she gets hot. Her basketball IQ and ability to control her speed help her get past defenders. Meanwhile, she can also make an impact on defense as she averaged 2.9 steals per game, which put her in the top 25 in the nation. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. JuJu WatkinsBy the time USC plays its season opener, it will have been about 19 months since Watkins tore her ACL during the second round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament. However, her comeback is one of the biggest storylines this season. Watkins is a modern wing whose skills allow her to play shooting guard or point guard. She is a three-level scorer, a strong playmaker and a versatile defender. Most notably, she helped the Trojans reach a level of success they hadn't seen since the '90s. 
Watkins set the NCAA Division I women's basketball freshman scoring record with 920 points during the 2023-24 season. In the process, she led the Trojans to their first Elite Eight appearance since 1994. The following year, she earned the 2024-25 Naismith Player of the Year award while averaging 23.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 2.2 steals and 1.8 blocks per game. It was hard to figure out where to rank Watkins since she's been out for so long, but her level of talent and what she showed before her injury makes her a player who should not be underestimated. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. Hannah HidalgoThe energy Hidalgo plays with every time she steps on the court is the definition of a "dawg." She might be an undersized guard, but you can't ever count her out. Hidalgo led the Fighting Irish all the way to the Elite Eight despite a major roster turnover last season. She dominated in the Sweet Sixteen victory against Vanderbilt with 31 points, 11 rebounds, 10 steals, seven assists and a block. She was just as impressive during the regular season, averaging 25.3 points, 6.9 rebounds, 5.2 assists, 5.6 steals per game. Hidalgo's efforts on offense made her the nation's third-leading scorer. Meanwhile, she also set a new Division I single season steals record -- an effort that earned her the Naismith Defensive Player of the Year award. As she begins her senior year, Hidalgo will be the only returning player for Notre Dame. A major rebuild like that usually leaves a lot of questions for a team, but with Hidalgo on the roster, the Fighting Irish are certainly in good hands.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Sarah StrongThe UConn star was named the 2026 Naismith Player of the Year because of her efficiency and how complete her game is. Throughout her sophomore season, Strong averaged 18.4 points per game as a three-level scorer. She shot 58.2% from the field and over 40% from 3-point range, while also registering 7.7 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 3.4 steals and 1.6 blocks per contest.To make those numbers even more impressive, coach Geno Auriemma revealed that Strong had not been 100% all season because she tweaked her Achilles tendon while playing 3x3 basketball for USA Basketball in Mongolia during the summer of 2025. Strong will likely be even more dangerous this upcoming season as she spent the summer resting. The talent is there, but this year will be all about growing as a leader and getting comfortable with the spotlight now that Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd – who she considers her mentors- are no longer around.

schema.headline: Ranking the 10 best women's college basketball players for 2026-27: Can anyone catch Sarah Strong? - CBS Sports

title: Florida State fires Mike Norvell: Big buyout can't save Seminoles coach after disastrous three-year stretch - CBS Sports
description: Norvell was 41-39 in seven seasons and fell to 3-5 in 2026 after Saturday's loss to Clemson
body:
Norvell was 41-39 in seven seasons and fell to 3-5 in 2026 after Saturday's loss to Clemson
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:39 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After months of speculation about Mike Norvell's job security, Florida State decided to make a change and fired Norvell in his seventh season as coach of the Seminoles, the university announced on Sunday. For weeks, the sense from those in and around Florida State was that Norvell might be safe due to his enormous $46 million buyout and an athletic department in flux. However, those factors couldn't save Norvell. "We have made the decision to change the leadership of our football program," FSU president Richard McCullough said in a statement. "We thank Mike Norvell for his commitment and service to Florida State and wish him and his family the very best. We understand the deep passion of Seminole fans and share their high expectations for this program. We are confident in Rick Stockstill's ability to provide steady leadership during this transition. We will conduct a thorough national search for the program's next leader, someone who embraces Florida State's tradition of championship athletics and our standard of excellence." 
        
            
                Mike Norvell buyout: What it cost Florida State to move on from football coach 8 games into 7th season
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Apparently, the final straw for the power brokers at Florida State was Saturday's 36-24 loss to Clemson at home. The Seminoles weren't competitive for much of the game, and the Doak Campbell Stadium crowd dwindled  in the second half. 
The optics of a "Fire Mike Norvell" banner flying over the stadium prior to kickoff certainly didn't help, even if Dabo Swinney came to Norvell's defense. Along with Norvell, Florida State also fired defensive coordinator Tony White, whose unit has surrendered 31.6 points per game.Former Florida State quarterback and current director of scouting Rick Stockstill will take over as interim coach. Stockstill spent 18 seasons at MTSU and led the Blue Raiders to an overall record of 113-11 with 10 bowl appearances.
Norvell's tenure filled with ups and downsFlorida State hired Norvell in 2020, and he made noticeable progress in each of his first four seasons on the job. That culminated in a 13-1 season in 2023 in which the Seminoles won the ACC Championship but were left out of the four-team College Football Playoff after quarterback Jordan Travis went down with a late season-ending injury. That year, Norvell won Bobby Dodd Coach of the Year and ACC Coach of the Year. Since then, it's been a steady spiral downward for Norvell and the program as a whole. The 2024 season began with high expectations, but big whiffs in the transfer portal resulted in a disastrous 2-10 campaign. Over the last two seasons, Florida State has been well behind the curve on the NIL market, and it's struggled to compete at a high level. Since the start of that miserable 2024 season, Norvell has led the Seminoles to a10-22 record with no tangible signs of progress. 
Perhaps a coaching change will prompt a bigger investment into NIL and help Florida State close the gap with some of the biggest spenders in the ACC and college football at large. Norvell exits Tallahassee with an overall record of 41-39, and based on his track record prior to the 2024 season, he will get opportunities elsewhere. Prior to his Florida State tenure, Norvell had a successful four-season run at Memphis in which he compiled a 38-16 record and an American Athletic Conference championship. Norvell never recovered from 2024 Despite the frustrating way in which the 2023 season ended, optimism was high in Tallahassee coming into the 2024 campaign. The Seminoles pulled in a highly-touted transfer class that ranked seventh in the country, according to the 247Sports Team Rankings. 
In addition to landing D.J. Uiagalelei, Norvell and his staff poached a handful of talented players from Alabama. Among them were receiver Malik Benson, defensive back Earl Little Jr. and offensive lineman TJ Ferguson. Despite those additions, the Noles cratered on both sides of the ball. They scored just 15.4 points per game while allowing 28.0 points per game. The result was a disastrous 2-10 season from which Norvell never recovered. After that point, the Seminoles fell behind their peers on the NIL market, both in terms of funding and evaluation. Although Florida State landed the No. 8 transfer class in 2025, it resulted in just five wins. This past offseason, the Seminoles tumbled to No. 28 in the transfer class rankings, and it especially misread the market at quarterback. 
Florida State brought in Ashton Daniels, who has struggled mightily, and the Noles are set to miss a bowl for the third consecutive season. That 2024 failure started a backslide that Norvell and his staff could never stop.  What will FSU's future look like? The firing of Norvell ends months of speculation about his job security, but there are still more questions than answers about Florida State at the moment. 
First of all, what will happen atop the athletic department? The school is still looking for a full-time athletic director after firing Michael Alford in September. According to CBS Sports' own Richard Johnson, Florida State wants to embrace the new era of college athletics and find an athletic director who can find creative ways to create revenue for the department. Better late than never. The second question is about the candidate list Florida State will compile. Will the Seminoles want to go the route of up-and-coming Group of Six coach, which is what led them to Norvell during the last coaching search. That path can certainly work. Just look at the last two coaches hired out of James Madison. However, will the power brokers prefer a coach with a track record of winning at the Power Four level? Poaching a sitting coach will be more expensive, and it's fair to wonder whether the school will be able to rally the financial support to make that happen. If it can, a steady hand could provide the type of stability this program has needed for the last few years.

title: AP Top 25 poll: Georgia climbs to No. 2 in college football rankings; Ohio State falls out of top 10 - CBS Sports
description: The Bulldogs are just behind No. 1 Miami in this week's AP Top 25
body:
The Bulldogs are just behind No. 1 Miami in this week's AP Top 25
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        On the heels of Week 9, there are a few teams on the move in the top 10 of the AP Top 25 poll. After its 27-8 blowout win over rival Florida, Georgia has climbed back up to No. 2 in the poll released Sunday.The Bulldogs were all over the place on defense, forcing four turnovers and returning one of them for a touchdown. Perhaps that will serve as a springboard for Georgia down the stretch as it hunts for another national title. On the other side of that rivalry game, Florida sank to No. 25 with a third loss on its resume. Elsewhere, the voters clearly weren't interested in giving the Buckeyes any grace for starting a freshman quarterback against the Trojans. Now with two losses on the season, Ohio State is running out of wiggle room, and its new AP poll ranking reflects that. USC, on the other hand, climbs back into the poll at No. 18 as it has new life heading into the home stretch.Utah was a beneficiary of Ohio State's drop, rising to No. 3, and this weekend's Holy War is officially locked in as a top-10 matchup with BYU coming in at No. 7.
Additionally, Saturday night's matchup between Notre Dame and Miami will be a top-four clash in South Bend. The Hurricanes remain at No. 1 after surviving a Halloween scare from North Carolina, and the Fighting Irish creep up to No. 4 on the strength of a dominant second half against Navy.The complete poll heading into Week 10 can be seen below.AP Top 25 pollRANKSCHOOLRECPTSLW1Miami (62)8-01,74012Georgia (7)7-11,64833Utah (1)8-01,54064Notre Dame7-11,47655UCLA8-01,47376Indiana8-11,44687BYU7-11,35888Kentucky7-11,25399Alabama6-21,1071010Texas6-21,0571111Ohio State6-21,0492012Ole Miss6-29531213Texas Tech7-19311314Wake Forest7-18981415LSU6-28141516Tennessee6-27191617Houston6-25901618USC7-25393119Missouri6-24751520Boise State7-14512021Iowa6-24012622New Mexico7-11792723South Carolina5-31631624Arizona6-21542225Florida5-39417Others receiving votes: Northwestern 79, Oregon 55, UTSA 43, SMU 27, Virginia Tech 12, Duke 10, Minnesota 8, Liberty 4, Oklahoma State 3, Louisville 1No sympathy for the BuckeyesIf you were wondering whether Ohio State would get the benefit of the doubt with Luke Fahey making his first career start in sloppy conditions, it did not. The Buckeyes now sit outside the top 10, and they still have some tricky games left the rest of the way.
Looking ahead, it will be very interesting to see how the College Football Playoff committee views this team on Tuesday night. Will the Buckeyes get any grace for that loss with star quarterback Julian Sayin on the shelf due to injury. The last time a star quarterback was hurt for a College Football Playoff contender, undefeated Florida State was left out of the field in 2023 because Jordan Travis was out for the season.Can Georgia break the No. 2 curse?The No. 2 spot has been dangerous over the last few weeks. The second-ranked team has lost in three consecutive weeks -- Notre Dame, BYU and Ohio State. Georgia will try to buck that trend, but it won't be easy.The Bulldogs have to go on the road to play Ole Miss, and there are lingering questions about their passing game despite a lopsided victory over Florida. If Georgia is going to become the first No. 2 team to win since Oct. 10 (also Georgia), it will have to do one of two things. Either the Bulldogs defense will have to bottle up Trinidad Chambliss in Oxford, or Gunner Stockton will have to make some big throws on offense.
History for New MexicoFollowing its win over San Jose, New Mexico has been ranked in the AP Top 25 poll for the first time in program history. It's a well-earned distinction for the Lobos after a 7-1 start has them eyeing a path to the College Football Playoff as the Group of Six participant. This is another feather in the cap of coach Jason Eck, who will be one of the hottest names on the coaching carousel this offseason.For now, the Lobos have to focus on running the table the rest of the way in hopes of supplanting Boise State as the highest-ranked Group of Six team.

After an offseason full of court cases with unresolved outcomes for dozens of players fighting for a fifth year of eligibility, actual basketball games will be the focus in the coming days and weeks to follow. Twenty of the preseason AP Top 25 teams will be in action on Monday, including two ranked-on-ranked matchups that will set the table for what should be a season full of intriguing storylines. Florida enters the season ranked No. 1 and seeks its second title in three years but will be tested early against in-state foe No. 14 Miami in Tampa.One of the final games of the night will see a former Pac-12 rivalry renewed when No. 5 Arizona faces No. 22 UCLA in Las Vegas. That game will represent the debut for two of the best freshmen in the sport: Arizona's Caleb Holt and UCLA's Nikola Kusturica. title: Jauan Jennings declined trade to return to 49ers after Vikings had framework set, per report - CBS Sports
description: The veteran receiver chose to stay with the undefeated Vikings over a reunion with Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy,
body:
The veteran receiver chose to stay with the undefeated Vikings over a reunion with Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy, despite having caught just four passes this season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026 NFL trade deadline has already been a dramatic one, as the Seattle Seahawks acquired an eight-time Pro Bowl offensive guard in Quenton Nelson, the Chicago Bears gave up two first-round picks for Tennessee Titans All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, and the Houston Texans reunited C.J. Stroud with Marvin Harrison Jr. This week, we also saw a player decline to be moved!According to Jay Glazer of Fox Sports, the Minnesota Vikings had a trade worked out that would send wide receiver Jauan Jennings back to the San Francisco 49ers. All Jennings had to do was hop on a FaceTime call with head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch and agree to return. However, Jennings declined, as he wants to stay in Minnesota! Jennings would rather stick with the undefeated Vikings, even if he's not a major part of Kyler Murray's passing attack. While Jennings has played 70.5% of offensive snaps this season, he's caught just FOUR passes for 43 yards in five games played. 
In five seasons with the 49ers, Jennings caught 210 passes for 2,581 yards and 22 touchdowns. He eventually became one of the most-trusted weapons for Brock Purdy, recording a career-high 975 yards receiving in 2024, and then a career-high nine touchdown receptions in 2025. Jennings ranked second on the team in receptions and receiving yards over the last two seasons, behind tight end George Kittle, and was tied with Kittle for the most receiving touchdowns over the past two seasons with 15. Jennings had more receptions (47) and receiving yards (546) on third down than any other 49er over the past two years, and led the team in red-zone targets, fourth-quarter targets and third-down targets. Jennings found himself in a contract dispute last summer, and even requested a trade out of San Francisco at one point. Eventually, he agreed to a modified deal based on incentives. After another impressive season in 2025, the former seventh-round pick out of Tennessee hit free agency expecting a payday. However, the market simply wasn't there, and Jennings agreed to a one-year deal with Minnesota worth up to $13 million.
The 49ers could have used Jennings, as their wide receiver room is banged up right now with Mike Evans dealing with rib and Achilles ailments and Deebo Samuel sidelined by a hamstring injury. However, Jennings wanted to remain in the NFC North.

        PITTSBURGH — Deshaun Watson took a big hit that temporarily forced him to exit the Browns' Week 8 showdown with the Steelers. Watson was replaced by Shedeur Sanders for the rest of the series but was back on the field for the start of Cleveland's next drive. Watson was hit high by Steelers defensive back Jaquan Brisker on the game's third play. Brisker was penalized for roughing the passer, giving the Browns a fresh set of downs. 
The drive ended with a pair of Steelers rookie defensive backs, Robert Spears-Jennings and Daylen Everett, combining to force and recover a fumble from Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. Watson, 31, has led the Browns to a 5-2 start and a share of first place in the AFC North. Watson captained the Browns to a 27-24 win over Pittsburgh back in Week 4. 
Sanders, a 2025 second-round pick, made the Pro Bowl as an alternate during his rookie season in 2025. His rookie debut included a win over the Steelers in Week 17.

title: Lions' Jack Campbell placed on backboard, carted off field after suffering serious injury - CBS Sports
description: The All-Pro linebacker suffered what appeared to be a serious injury vs. the Vikings
body:
The All-Pro linebacker suffered what appeared to be a serious injury vs. the Vikings
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:13 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field after appearing to suffer a serious injury during the team's Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.Following the 19-15 victory, Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters he had no further information on Jack's status, other than that he was receiving medical care.On the first play of the fourth quarter, Campbell and teammate Eric O'Neill combined to tackle Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. Campbell then went limp. While lying prone, he was seen moving his head up and down and pulling his body forward a couple of inches before trainers reached him. After about 10 minutes, Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field. 
The Lions announced that Campbell was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury. It was an emotional scene at Ford Field. The entire Lions team went over to see their teammate off, while the defense gathered for a moment to rally after seeing one of their leaders go down. 
In seven games this season, Campbell recorded 57 tackles, two QB hits and a fumble recovery. Just six months ago, he signed a four-year, $81 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid off-ball linebackers in the NFL. 
Campbell was selected with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Iowa, just six selections after the Lions drafted running back Jahmyr Gibbs. The 26-year-old had a career year in 2025, recording 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles and four passes defended. He was named a First Team All-Pro and earned his first Pro Bowl bid.

title: Lamar Jackson headed for injured reserve: Ravens QB to undergo surgery after injuring thumb vs. Bills - CBS Sports
description: Jackson made his first start on Sunday after missing the last three games
body:
Jackson made his first start on Sunday after missing the last three games
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:55 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Baltimore Ravens probably feel like they're living in a nightmare right now. In Lamar Jackson's return to the field on Sunday, the two-time NFL MVP got knocked out of the game after suffering a thumb injury on Baltimore's first offensive play against the Buffalo Bills. Following the Ravens' 36-10 loss, the news went from bad to worse with head coach Jesse Minter revealing that Jackson would be placed on injured reserve. "That will be a surgery deal," Minter said. "He'll go to IR."Putting Jackson on IR means he'll miss at least four games. Here's a look at Baltimore's upcoming schedule: Week 9: Jaguars (Thursday night)Week 10: ChargersWeek 11: at PanthersWeek 12: at TexansWeek 13: Bye Week 14: Buccaneers
With Jackson now on injured reserve, the earliest he can return is for that Week 14 game against the Bucs on Dec. 13. Jackson has already missed three games this season due to injury, and this will bring his total to at least seven. The thumb injury happened on Baltimore's first offensive play of the game. On a first-and-10 play, Jackson threw a pass to Zay Flowers, but as he threw the ball, his hand hit a defender's arm, and after that happened, Jackson was in immediate pain. 
Jackson clearly didn't feel right, because he quickly ran to the sideline, and at that point, the Ravens' training staff took him into Baltimore's locker room at Highmark Stadium. 
The showdown between Jackson and Josh Allen was supposed to be one of the highlights in Week 8, but instead, it turned into a blowout win for Buffalo after Jackson left the game. The Ravens have already played three games without Jackson this year, and if those were any indication, things could get ugly over the next few weeks. With Jackson on the field during their first four games, the Ravens averaged 29.8 points per game while going 3-1. However, with Jackson out over the past three weeks, they went just 1-2 while averaging just 17.7 points per game. And now, you can add another loss to that tally in a game where the Ravens managed to score just 10 points. 
For Thursday's game against Jacksonville, it's still not clear who the starting QB will be. Not only did Jackson get hurt, but Tyler Huntley also had to leave the game after injuring his toe. If Huntley isn't ready to return, that means QB Joe Fagnano will be getting the first start of his career. Fagnano, an undrafted rookie out of UConn, went 10-of-12 for 91 yards with an interception while playing about 2.5 quarters against the Bills.
        
            
                Who is Ravens' Joe Fagnano? Baltimore turns to third QB after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
For Jackson, there's no guarantee that he'll return as soon as he's eligible to come off IR. A thumb injury on the right hand is a brutal one for a quarterback because it impacts their ability to grip the football. Jackson will need that to fully heal before he can return, and since he has to undergo surgery, he likely won't be back on the field until late December. 
At 4-4, the Ravens will need to keep their head above water until then, or it could be a lost season for Baltimore.

title: Who is Ravens' Joe Fagnano? Baltimore turns to third QB after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries - CBS Sports
description: Baltimore is down to its third-string quarterback, an undrafted rookie
body:
Baltimore is down to its third-string quarterback, an undrafted rookie
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:51 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Ravens' quarterback issues went from awful to somehow even worse in a hurry in a crucial Week 8 meeting against the Bills. After Lamar Jackson, in his first game back from an ankle injury, injured his thumb on Baltimore's first offensive play of the game, backup Tyler Huntley got hurt in the second quarter. The Ravens had to turn to emergency third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano, a rookie undrafted free agent out of UConn.Jackson hit his thumb on Gregory Rousseau and immediately went to the locker room. Huntley, who started the Ravens' previous three games with Jackson sidelined, then got his foot caught/rolled up on by Ed Oliver.
Huntley is officially questionable to return. In his place, Fagnano finished 10-of-12 for 91 yards with an interception while playing about 2.5 quarters against the Bills.Who is Joe Fagnano?Though Fagnano is making his NFL debut Sunday, he has played a lot of football. A rare 25-year-old rookie, Fagnano started his collegiate career as a walk-on at Maine, an FCS program, in 2019. He earned the backup quarterback job — and a scholarship — quickly, though. Like his NFL debut, his college debut came after the starter got hurt. One week later, in his first collegiate start, Fagnano threw five touchdown passes in an upset win over FBS program Liberty.
The Black Bears only played four games in the 2020 season due to COVID-19, and Fagnano got hurt in 2021 and only played in four games. After a solid 2022 season, he transferred to UConn.After suffering a season-ending shoulder injury two games into his debut season at UConn, Fagnano played most of 2024. He got on NFL radars with an outstanding 2025 that included 28 passing touchdowns, one interception and 3,448 passing yards.
The Ravens invited Fagnano to a rookie tryout, where he beat out Diego Pavia for an opportunity to spend the summer with Baltimore. He capitalized with a strong preseason that included a nearly 75% completion percentage, three touchdowns and one interception.
Now, all of a sudden, he's trying to halt Baltimore's two-game losing streak. According to the CBS broadcast, running back Justice Hill would be the emergency quarterback to the emergency quarterback if Fagnano gets injured as well.

title: College football AP Top 25 rankings: New Mexico cracking poll for first time among things voters got right - CBS Sports
description: The last meaningful AP Poll of the season was revealing on Sunday
body:
The last meaningful AP Poll of the season was revealing on Sunday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Pour one out for Jason Eck and the Lobos after New Mexico's first AP Top 25 ranking in program history to highlight Sunday's Week 10 edition.Days out from the initial College Football Playoff rankings reveal, New Mexico is in the thick of the Group of Six auto-bid hunt on the strength of five straight wins following its only loss of the season, a 14-6 loss at Oklahoma on Sept. 19. The Lobos come in at No. 22, three spots behind G6 frontrunner Boise State this week.For the first time this season, it feels like AP voters kept a close eye on Saturday's action throughout the rankings, spitting out a poll — we feel — will look awfully similar to Tuesday's reveal of the first CFP rankings of the season.
        
            
                AP Top 25 poll: Georgia climbs to No. 2 in college football rankings; Ohio State falls out of top 10
                
                    Austin Nivison                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Here's three things voters got right entering the final month of the regular season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    1. Ohio State is not the team that beat IndianaThose expecting the Buckeyes to be the highest-ranked two-loss team in the first CFP rankings after Saturday's 30-18 setback at USC will be disappointed if this latest AP Poll is any indication. Properly docked for defensive issues and faulty execution from an array of pass-catchers, Ohio State is stinging after its second loss and fourth overall in its last 10 games under Ryan Day. Losing Julian Sayin to a season-ending arm injury is bad news for a team that looked like the Big Ten frontrunner recently after holding off Indiana, only to now being another loss away from potentially missing the bracket altogether. This was well done from AP voters this week, pushing Ohio State back nine spots to No. 11. Jeremiah Smith's Heisman hopes have taken a hit, too.Buckeyes' remaining slateSaturday, vs. OregonNov. 14, vs. NorthwesternNov. 21, at NebraskaNov. 28, vs. Michigan
                            
    
                                                
                    
    2. South Carolina has entered the chat The highest-ranked of two three-loss teams in the poll, the Gamecocks have won three straight games since starting the SEC slate 0-3 under Shane Beamer and look eerily similar to the program's 2024 squad that nearly reached the CFP with a red-hot second half. There's a chance South Carolina could force its way into the conversation by winning out, which would include victories over Georgia and Clemson down the stretch. 
The Gamecocks currently hold two top 25 wins (Florida, Tennessee) and led eighth-ranked Kentucky by 17 points back in September before faltering in overtime. Voters are keeping up with LaNorris Sellers and this unstoppable offense in recent weeks and South Carolina resembles a team most expected would be an at-large CFP contender in the SEC back in August.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    3. Voters finally notice MissouriThe Tigers moved up four spots inside the top 20 to No. 19 following losses from a few teams ahead of them and a convincing, rain-soaked 34-10 victory at Arkansas. It was a much-needed bounce back for Eli Drinkwitz's squad following a 28-point loss at Ole Miss earlier this month and featured the return of Ahmad Hardy in the backfield. As it stands, the Tigers have one ranked win (Florida) and get three opportunities against top-10 competition in consecutive weeks beginning Saturday against Texas as a narrow home underdog. Often undervalued — borderline ignored — this season by voters, Missouri has put itself in position to control its own CFP destiny the rest of the way. Quarterback Austin Simmons ranks in the top tier of the SEC's passing leaders this fall with 1,952 yards, 16 touchdowns and two interceptions while the Tigers have the fifth-best scoring defense in the conference despite losing heavy talent replacement this offseason, including edge rusher Damon Wilson II to Miami.

title: Jonathan Taylor trade rumors: Colts not actively shopping around star running back before deadline - CBS Sports
description: However, in a meeting with ownership, Taylor was not given any assurances that a deal would not happen, according
body:
However, in a meeting with ownership, Taylor was not given any assurances that a deal would not happen, according to CBS Sports' Aditi Kinkhabwala
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:42 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Jonathan Taylor is the belle of the ball as the NFL circles the Nov. 10 trade deadline. After the Colts spent the past week beginning what many believe is a full teardown, the star running back's status and uncertain future in Indianapolis have taken center stage. While a deal can't be ruled out, it doesn't appear as if Indy has a massive appetite to move him. "After trading away two captains and two pillars of their club in DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson, the Colts are, of course, getting phone calls asking about the availability of Taylor," CBS Sports' Aditi Kinkhabwala reported on Sunday. "But I have been assured by the Colts that they are not soliciting offers for the running back and that they are not actively seeking to move him." Kinkhabwala continued, saying that Taylor had a meeting with owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon this week in which the two discussed the back's future with the team. Irsay-Gordon reportedly "didn't give him any assurances that he is definitely going to stay on the team." For his part, Taylor reaffirmed to Irsay-Gordon his love for the organization. 
Earlier this week, the Colts traded Nelson to the Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, while sending Buckner to San Francisco for a 2027 fourth-rounder. When it comes to Taylor, the asking price will probably be larger than those returns, as he remains one of the top running backs in the NFL. 
This latest report from Kinkhabwala suggests they'd need to be blown away in order for the organization to pull the trigger on a trade. Taylor, a 2020 second-round pick out of Wisconsin, has spent the first seven years of his career in Indy. Last season, the 27-year-old led the NFL in rushing touchdowns (18) and topped 1,000 yards rushing for the fourth time in his career. Entering Week 8, Taylor has 587 yards rushing and a league-high eight rushing touchdowns. 
On Saturday, ESPN reported that the slew of teams interested in Taylor includes the Broncos, Packers, Vikings, Giants, and Seahawks.

title: Mike Norvell fired: Buyout, contract details as Florida State ousts coach in 7th season - CBS Sports
description: The Seminoles are looking at a hefty payout for Norvell after moving on from their seventh-year coach
body:
The Seminoles are looking at a hefty payout for Norvell after moving on from their seventh-year coach
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Florida State fired seventh-year coach Mike Norvell on Sunday, parting ways following the Seminoles' 36-24 home loss to Clemson on Saturday that featured countless empty seats during a multi-possession game in the fourth quarter.The team's third consecutive ACC loss was the 17th setback for Norvell in his last 21 games against league competition, a horrid stretch that kept him on the hot seat each of the last two years.Norvell's buyout is estimated just under $49 million — roughly 85% of his remaining salary through a contract running through the 2031 season — which would be the third-biggest payout in college football history. That figure is behind only the $77 million paid to Jimbo Fisher at Texas A&M and LSU's $54 million check to Brian Kelly last cycle. Norvell's remaining deal is subject to mitigation and could be offset and reduced if he lands another coaching job.
Norvell signed a lucrative contract extension following the 2023 season, when the Seminoles went undefeated in the regular season and won the ACC title -- only to be snubbed from the College Football Playoff due to quarterback injuries. With Nick Saban retiring at Alabama that same cycle, Norvell found just the right leverage to get a massive extension from Florida State that thrust him onto the list of the top 10 highest-paid coaches in the country. That contract has aged like milk as the Seminoles went 7-17 over the 2024 and 2025 seasons, which made 2026 a make-or-break year in Tallahassee for Norvell. Norvell's contract, buyout detailsNorvell's extension after the 2023 season may go down as one of the most regrettable deals a program has made in recent memory, as it tacked on two extra years through 2031 and raised his salary by more than $2 million per year. That made it prohibitively expensive for Florida State to move on from Norvell, and the calculus in Tallahassee coming into the 2026 campaign was measuring whether it's worth waiting for the buyout to drop or risk finding out there's still further to dig before hitting rock bottom.
Norvell is set to earn $10.3 million in salary for the 2026 season, and has five years and $54.75 million remaining on his contract after this year. After his in-season firing on Sunday, the Seminoles owe Norvell just over $48.6 million -- 85% of the remaining five years plus $3 million and an additional $750,000 as part of a recently-renegotiated buyout agreement. That would be just below the amount Penn State was scheduled to pay James Franklin when they fired him last year, but Franklin and Penn State agreed to reduce the $49 million buyout to just $9 million as he was set to become Virginia Tech's new coach. 
Norvell may not have the same immediate opportunities as Franklin, and the Seminoles can't bank on such a drastic reduction in cost. As such, it's a considerable financial commitment from Florida State's boosters to move on from Norvell, but one they were willing to pay to cut ties entering November.
